In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[graph theory]], the '''Harries&ndash;Wong graph'''<!--
, named after ?????? Haries and ?????? Wong, 
--> is a 3-[[regular graph|regular]] [[undirected graph]] with 70 vertices and 105 edges.<ref>{{MathWorld|urlname=Harries-WongGraph|title= Harries&ndash;Wong Graph}}</ref>

The Harries&ndash;Wong graph has [[chromatic number]] 2, [[chromatic index]] 3, radius 6, diameter 6, girth 10 and is [[Hamiltonian graph|Hamiltonian]]. It is also a 3-[[k-vertex-connected graph|vertex-connected]] and 3-[[k-edge-connected graph|edge-connected]] [[planar graph|non-planar]] [[cubic graph]]. It has [[book thickness]] 3 and [[queue number]] 2.<ref>Jessica Wolz, ''Engineering Linear Layouts with SAT''. Master Thesis, University of Tübingen, 2018</ref>

The characteristic polynomial of the Harries–Wong graph is

: <math>(x-3) (x-1)^4 (x+1)^4 (x+3) (x^2-6) (x^2-2) (x^4-6x^2+2)^5 (x^4-6x^2+3)^4 (x^4-6x^2+6)^5. \, </math>

==History==
In 1972, A. T. Balaban published a (3-10)-cage graph, a cubic graph that has as few vertices as possible for girth 10.<ref>A. T. Balaban, A trivalent graph of girth ten, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 12, 1&ndash;5. 1972.</ref> It was the first (3-10)-cage discovered but it was not unique.<ref>Pisanski, T.; Boben, M.; Marušič, D.; and Orbanić, A. "The Generalized Balaban Configurations." Preprint. 2001. [http://citeseer.ist.psu.edu/448980.html].</ref>

The complete list of (3-10)-cages and the proof of minimality was given by O'Keefe and Wong in 1980.<ref>M. O'Keefe and P.K. Wong, A smallest graph of girth 10 and valency 3, J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 29 (1980) 91&ndash;105.</ref> There exist three distinct (3-10)-cage graphs—the [[Balaban 10-cage]], the [[Harries graph]] and the Harries&ndash;Wong graph.<ref>[[John Adrian Bondy|Bondy, J. A.]] and [[U. S. R. Murty|Murty, U. S. R.]] Graph Theory with Applications. New York: North Holland, p. 237, 1976.</ref> Moreover, the Harries&ndash;Wong graph and Harries graph are [[Spectral graph theory|cospectral graphs]].
